To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
it is technically feasible to replace the existing, outdated Hungarian electricity system with one that is based on renewable energy sources and which is more independent from foreign sources.

it is possible to achieve a 25–30% share of renewable energy in the electricity generation of Hungary by 2030, and that the country could become independent of non-domestic electricity imports by the same year.

• It is technically feasible, with no significant changes in the structure of the Hungarian electricity generating system to replace the obsolete capacity with renewable sources and to reduce the dependence on imported electricity and fossil fuels; • It is possible to achieve a significant reduction of CO2 emissions; • The costs are not significantly higher than in the official scenarios; • There is no reason for the government to delay the introduction of renewable energy technologies and energy independence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a sustainable, environmentally friendly, and independent electricity system for Hungary, based on the current situation and the official plans for the future.
the following issues: the development of an electricity system for Hungary which is more independent of imported energy and more environmentally friendly than official forecasts.

the development of a new, environmentally friendly electricity system for Hungary; the development of a system based on renewable sources; the development of an electricity system which is less dependent upon imported electricity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Hungary has the potential to become an electricity exporter, with a high share of renewable energy sources, without the need for any new nuclear power plants, but this would require a significant change in the current official policy and strategy.
it is possible to build a sustainable, environmentally friendly and energy independent Hungarian electricity system, but that the current political decision makers are not willing to do so.
the current official scenario is not sustainable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is possible for Hungary to achieve energy independence and to have a significant proportion of renewable energy in its electricity generation system.
Hungary's electricity system could be transformed into one that is less reliant on fossil fuels, less reliant on imports, more environmentally friendly, more competitive and more secure.
Hungary could be energy-independent, if it would use the full potential of renewable energy sources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Hungarian electricity system can be developed in a way that would be less dependent on imported energy sources and would be more environment friendly.
it is not necessary to make major changes to the existing system, and that the introduction of renewable energy is feasible.
it is technically and economically feasible to develop an electricity system in Hungary that is less dependent on foreign sources of energy.
